# `check_pa_alt`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Check whether the mount tilt matches the site latitude closely enough for equatorial polar alignment.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / established (strict, 64-bit build; location/time cache refresh and logging); 32-bit build probable. Behaviourally a getter. |
| Side-effect tier | B |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0xb61a0 (64-bit build); LoadUserLocation (64-bit build) |

No parameters are read. Returns result.is_valid. Special case: in equatorial mode, if the user location cannot be loaded, the handler appends an error and then also appends the result (is_valid true), so one reply carries both error and result members and two code members (the failure code, then 0). A parser that keeps the last duplicate sees code 0 while the error string remains; clients SHOULD treat the presence of error as failure. Out-of-range location is reported with code 204; unassigned failures fall to 207. An invalid orientation is is_valid false, not an error.

Side effects: May refresh the shared user-location and time cache from configuration. No mount motion or setting write. Full command-socket calls also incur the shared diagnostic (logging) writes; this is why the strict grade is MUTATOR even for the read-only calls.

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 204 | Equatorial mode and the configured location is outside longitude (-360.1, 360.1) or latitude (-90.1, 90.1); the reply also carries result.is_valid true | `out of limit` |
| 207 | Equatorial mode and the location could not be read for another reason with no code assigned; the reply also carries result | `fail to operate` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: method missing or not a string | `invalid request` |

Other configuration-read failures can carry other, unassigned codes.

## Example

Request, request:

```json
{"id":33,"method":"check_pa_alt"}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"check_pa_alt","result":{"is_valid":false},"code":0,"id":33}
```

Reply, bad-location:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"check_pa_alt","error":"out of limit","code":204,"id":34}
```
